claims: Solver/checker separation: if every checker-accepted decision satisfies the specification and every solver output is checker-accepted, every solver output is specification-valid.
Equivalent checkers preserve solver soundness when acceptance behavior is identical.
Sound solver stages compose when the intermediate specifications imply the end specification.
Witness payloads are non-authoritative: for a sound solver, validity depends on the accepted decision, not on trusting the witness by itself.
Cross-surface extraction is bounded by one shared verified-benefit budget after overlap removal.
Non-positive shared verified budget forces all nonnegative settlement, liquidity, oracle, and governance takes to zero.
Role-collapse release requires execute authority, live-execution capability, bounded loss, positive shared budget, and cross-surface take below that shared budget.
Advisory-only, stage-only, no-live-execution, zero-loss, and non-positive-budget cases fail closed for execute-class role-collapse release.
proof_method: Boolean and Prop checker acceptance decomposition
solver-stage composition by matching optional outputs
integer budget inequalities over shared cross-surface benefit
capability-rank case analysis reused from the advisory capability model

boundaries: This is a proof-level interface theorem. Runtime integrations still need to map concrete solver, checker, decision, and witness types into the abstract fields.
The solver/checker theorem proves accepted solver outputs are spec-valid; it does not prove checker completeness unless a separate completeness proof is supplied.
Cross-surface budget arithmetic assumes faithful measurement of verified benefits, overlap, and requested extraction values.
Role-collapse release safety composes existing capability and budget models; it does not prove a full equilibrium for post-AGI reward systems.
